title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 6th District
area: Central New Jersey, including parts of Middlesex, Monmouth, Ocean, and Somerset counties.

context.text: Incumbent Frank Pallone Jr. won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary with 65.7% of the vote against John Hsu and Katie Bansil. Hillary Herzig won the Republican primary unopposed.
The Cook Political Report's Partisan Voter Index rates the district D+5.

summary.text: Frank Pallone Jr. is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 6th Congressional District, first elected to the U.S. House in 1988. A Long Branch native and attorney, he previously served on the Long Branch City Council and in the New Jersey Senate. He is the top Democrat on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, which he chaired from 2019 to 2023, and his official biography highlights health care, environmental, and consumer-protection work.

background.text: Born in Long Branch, New Jersey, where, according to his official biography, he began his political career and still lives.
Earned a B.A. from Middlebury College in 1973, an M.A. from Tufts University in 1974, and a J.D. from Rutgers University in 1978; Ballotpedia lists his profession as attorney.
Elected to the Long Branch City Council in 1982 and to the New Jersey Senate, representing the Monmouth County coastline, in 1983; he was re-elected to the state Senate in 1987.

Elected to the U.S. House on November 8, 1988, from New Jersey's former 3rd District. After the 1992 redistricting he was elected in the 6th District, which his office describes as covering most of Middlesex County and the Bayshore and oceanfront areas of Monmouth County.
Chaired the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Health in 2010, when, according to his official biography, he played a key role in authoring the Affordable Care Act.

Chaired the full House Energy and Commerce Committee during the 117th Congress (2021-2022), and is now its top Democrat; the committee's jurisdiction includes health care, energy, environment, commerce, food and drug safety, consumer protection, and communications and technology.

His office credits him with legislation giving the Food and Drug Administration additional oversight tools over cosmetics, included in the fiscal year 2023 federal spending bill, and with efforts to ban offshore drilling and ocean dumping off New Jersey's coast.
Married his wife Sarah in 1992; they have three adult children, according to his official biography.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (ex officio on its Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Environment; Health; Oversight and Investigations; Communications and Technology; and Energy subcommittees), which he chaired 2019-2023 and previously served as Ranking Member (2015-2016).

Introduced the bipartisan Family Vaccine Protection Act with Rep. Kim Schrier, intended to keep HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. from unilaterally changing the childhood immunization schedule and to require the schedule to follow the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices' science-based recommendations.
Pushed for stronger federal consumer protections against robocalls and robotexts.
Joined hospital leaders at a Saint Peter's University Hospital "Save Our Hospitals" event warning about the effects of Republican-passed Medicaid cuts.

candidates.name: Hillary Herzig
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary unopposed with 100% of the vote.

summary.text: Hillary Herzig is the Republican nominee for New Jersey's 6th Congressional District. According to her campaign website, she is a Monmouth County resident and spouse of a U.S. Army veteran who spent 2010-2025 as a civil servant in public-safety, military-family, veterans', and national-security roles. She is running on parental rights in education, lower taxes, medical freedom, and immigration reform.

background.text: According to her campaign website, attended elementary, middle, and high school in New Jersey; describes herself as a Monmouth County resident, mother of three, and spouse of a U.S. Army veteran.
Earned a Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice from Florida Atlantic University (2006-2010).
Career civil servant (2010-2025): Executive Assistant to the Chief of Police in Key West, Florida, then a Special Security Representative with the U.S. Army National Ground Intelligence Center.
While stationed in Germany as an Army spouse, taught military dependent children through the Department of Defense Education Activity.

Later worked at the Veterans Administration, USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, and the Department of Homeland Security's U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, in asylum mission support and personnel security.

Her campaign website also lists experience as an artist and business owner, a veteran caregiver, and a children's book author, and says she began pursuing a master's degree in political science with a public policy concentration at American Military University in 2025.
According to her campaign website, her family traveled the country in 2022 before returning to New Jersey to raise their children.

priorities.text: Parental rights and transparency in education.
Lower taxes and economic relief for working families.
National sovereignty and what she calls fair, intelligent immigration reform.

positions.summary: Campaigns on national sovereignty and immigration reform, listing it among her core priorities.

candidates.researchNotes: Herzig has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; positions drawn from her campaign website.
